text:
**My top pick for most campers is a 300 Wh-class station.** That size covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP for a weekend, and it's light enough to carry easily. If you want to run bigger appliances, step up to roughly 1,000 Wh.

## Light and simple (weekend trips)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** (~$249): 288 Wh, 8.3 lb, 300 W output. PowerStationGearLab ranks it best overall for camping. I don't have a direct buy link in my results, so see the [review and Amazon link](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/).
- **[BLUETTI Elite 30 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2)** ($289.99, or $275.50 with code AFF5OFF): 288 Wh, 600 W output, 4.3 kg. One caveat is that its solar input maxes out at 28 V, so many 100 W+ folding panels won't work with it. It's also not airline-legal.
- **Anker SOLIX C300** (~$199) and **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** (~$269-299, 600 W) are other good picks in the same class, per the same [PowerStationGearLab guide](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/).
- **[Tenergy T320](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-t320-300wh-power-station)** ($225.99): the lightest budget option at 3.7 kg. It outputs only 200 W, so no kettles or heaters, and a wall recharge takes about 8 hours.

## More power (a fridge, a cooking appliance, or longer trips)
- **[BLUETTI AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)** ($499, or $474.05 with code AFF5OFF): 1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, about 16 kg, and 500 W solar input. It's the best all-rounder in Dealectric's records. The price is for the station alone, and it has no expansion port.
- **[ALLPOWERS P1800](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh)** ($439, or $395.10 with code ALLPOWERS26): 1,024 Wh and 1,800 W for less money. Its warranty is 24 months, and the store page contradicts itself on cycle count.
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** (under $530 at last check) is OutdoorGearLab's best value pick. The **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** (39 lbs, under $900) is their pick for multi-day off-grid trips. See their [full test](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station).

## Notes
- Dealectric's list only covers Bluetti, Tenergy, and ALLPOWERS. It has no Jackery, EcoFlow, or Anker, so those come from the review sites.
- The Dealectric links are affiliate links, and the review sites also earn commissions.
- Prices and discount codes change, so confirm them at checkout.
- A CPAP typically uses 30-60 Wh a night, and turning off the humidifier cuts that a lot.

If you tell me what you'll power and how many nights you'll be out, I can narrow this to one pick.
